summary.one_liner: GANSpace is a research codebase that uses PCA in GAN activation space to find interpretable, layer-wise controls for image synthesis in models such as BigGAN, StyleGAN and StyleGAN2.
summary.what_it_does: The repository provides code accompanying the NeurIPS 2020 paper of the same name. It applies Principal Components Analysis to GAN activations to find latent directions that correspond to visual edits such as viewpoint, aging, lighting, and time of day. It includes versions of BigGAN, StyleGAN and StyleGAN2 modified to accept per-layer latent vectors. An interactive.py script lets a user explore and save edits, and a visualize.py script renders principal components, optionally as videos. Jupyter notebooks are included to regenerate the paper's figures. Supported models named in the README are ProGAN, BigGAN-512/256/128, StyleGAN, and StyleGAN2.
use_cases: Find interpretable edit directions in a pretrained GAN
Explore BigGAN or StyleGAN2 latent space interactively
Create videos of principal component edits
Reproduce figures from the GANSpace paper
Add a new GAN model to a PCA-based editing pipeline
Import StyleGAN weights from TensorFlow checkpoints
how_to_run: See the setup instructions referenced in the README (no explicit install commands given)
stack: TensorFlow (only for optional StyleGAN checkpoint import)
notable: Layer-wise latent edits: applies PCA edit directions at chosen network layers, StyleGAN-like control of BigGAN
Includes modified BigGAN, StyleGAN and StyleGAN2 code supporting per-layer latent vectors
Jupyter notebooks reproduce each main paper figure
Documented wrapper interface (BaseModel) for integrating new models
caveats: Interactive viewer may freeze on startup on Ubuntu 18.04 (workaround described in README)
A landscape StyleGAN model from ArtBreeder is used in the paper but cannot be distributed with the repo
Setup is delegated to separate instructions; StyleGAN checkpoint import requires TensorFlow 1.x and manual code edits
